text: A pack is a candidate version of this service's own access model: an ordered set of PERMISSION, SCOPE and MASKING rows with a packVersion, an ownerRole and a capabilityArea. The check is served by POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks and the read by GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks, with the schemas PackCheck, PackRow, DefectItem, PackCheckAnswer and PackCheckSummary, the check codes PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK, the verdicts ACCEPTED and RETURNED, one defect item per failing row and check, and one verdict per packVersion of an owner role.
why: No source names a pack operation of this service, the rows a pack carries or the codes a verdict uses; the legacy story's endpoints are another key's and the FSD gives an intent and no operation. The shape is derived from the three tables this service owns and from the requirement that access outside the matrix is refused and recorded.

text: PC-SCP refuses a pack that names one role in two SCOPE rows and a scope row whose role code no `role` row holds. A pack may narrow or restate a scope and may not leave two scopes in force for one role.
why: No source states the scope rule of a pack. REQ-ACA-009 makes scope the unit a user is filtered by, so two scope rows for one role is a state the matrix cannot answer, and the check refuses it at submission rather than at load.

text: The personal capability areas of PC-MSK, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the pack version label shape are parameter rows of rwb-case read through the parameters contract of DP-06 with the version in force; the letters a permission row may name are the model constant C, R, U, D and A of the `permission.letters` column, because the key's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
why: No source names the parameter rows or their values, and the run forbids writing a business value in code. The letter set is not a free value: it is the declared domain of a varchar(5) column of this service's own model, so it is read as a model constant rather than as a list of values the service does not hold.

text: The submit authorises Rules and parameters C, held by RW-COE, and the read authorises Rules and parameters R, held by the owner role a pack is returned to (RW-LITOFF and RW-AUDIT). The key carries no approve leg: the approval of a matrix version belongs to the administration stories of this service.
why: Two sources disagree. The legacy permission table gives C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-LITOFF R only, and the story's persona is a litigation officer while the story has no approval step. The split keeps both sources: the preparing role submits, the owning role reads what was returned.

text: The check is request-driven: a pack is checked when it is submitted, no Temporal Schedule and no workflow starts it, and the task a person needs is the returned-packs list of SCR-39. VR-P4-025-1, the ACE data-product freshness rule of FSD P4 v3 A2.25.3.1, is not implemented here because the key carries no DP-05.
why: FSD P4 v3 makes the step unattended on an ACE batch, an event or a timer, while the key's pattern list carries no DP-05 and no DP-10, the service owns no event and its only Schedule is another story's. The two cannot both hold, and the metadata is the binding statement of the run.
